q: 1. International Civil Aviation Organization (I.G.A.O.) was set up at Montreal (Canada), in ...........
explain: ICAO was established on April 4, 1947, following the ratification of the Convention on International Civil Aviation (Chicago Convention).

q: 2. Pick up the correct statement from the following ...........
options: the speed of the aircraft relative to the ground, is called cruising speed
the speed of the aircraft relative to wind, is called air speed
when wind is blowing the direction of the flight, air speed is less than cruising speed
explain: Cruising speed is the efficient speed for long distances; air speed is relative to the air mass; and tailwinds make ground speed (cruising speed in this context) higher than airspeed.

q: 3. Pick up the component not applicable to aeroplanes ...........
explain: Wings provide lift, engines provide power, and the air screw (propeller) provides thrust; all are standard components of traditional aeroplanes.

q: 4. Pick up the incorrect statement from the following ...........
options: in single engine aeroplanes, the engine is provided in the nose of the aircraft
in double engine aeroplanes, one engine on either wing is placed symmetrically
in three engine aeroplanes, two engines are placed on both wings and one engine is placed in the tail
explain: In many three-engine configurations (like the DC-10), one engine is in the tail and the other two are under the wings, but the statement 'on both wings' (plural) implies multiple per wing or a specific symmetry not universally 'incorrect' except in the context of standard textbook definitions for sub-engineers.

q: 5. The fuselage includes ...........
explain: The fuselage is the main body of the aircraft that holds the crew, passengers, cargo, and connects the wings and tail assembly.

q: 6. Pick up the correct statement from the following ...........
options: air screw converts the energy given by the engine into speed
the propellers which are driven by turbine engines, are technically called turbo-props
the aircrafts which obtain the thrust directly from turbine engine, are called turbo-jets
explain: These are the standard technical definitions for propellers (air screws), turboprop engines, and turbojet engines.

q: 7. According to the International Civil Aviation Organization (I.C.A.O.), the runway lengths of aerodromes, have been coded by ...........
explain: ICAO uses a code system (1-4) for length and letters (A-E) for wingspan/wheel span; textbooks often refer to the first five letters (A, B, C, D, E) for airport classification.

q: 8. According to the International Civil Aviation Organization (I.G.A.O.) the strength of runway pavements, have been coded by ...........
explain: ICAO pavement strength is often categorized by numbers in older technical manuals or specifically through the ACN-PCN numerical system.

q: 9. The Maximum length and pavement strength of the runway is that of ...........
explain: In the ICAO coding system, 'A' represents the longest runway length and '1' represents the highest pavement strength category.

q: 10. Pick up the correct statement from the following ...........
options: minimum turning radius of aircrafts decides the size of the apron and the radius of the curves at taxi-ends
take off and landing distances for an aircraft, determine the minimum runway length
the length of the normal haul of the air craft decides the frequency of operation
explain: All these factors are fundamental design criteria in airport engineering for determining spatial requirements and infrastructure capacity.

q: 11. The thickness design of the pavement, is decided on the load carried by ...........
explain: The main landing gear carries approximately 90-95% of the aircraft weight, making it the primary factor for pavement thickness design.

q: 12. The maximum value of the angle of turning of the nose gear large jet aircrafts, is limited to ...........
explain: For large jet aircraft, the nose gear steering angle is typically limited to 60 degrees to prevent excessive tire scrubbing and mechanical stress.

q: 13. The distance between main gears is 10 m, and the distance of nose gear from centre of main gears is 30 m. If the angle of turning is 60°, the distance of centre of rotation from the nearer main gear, is ...........
explain: Using trigonometry for the turning radius: $R = b \cdot \cot(\theta)$. Distance from the center of rotation to the nearer gear involves subtracting half the gear tread.

q: 14. Wing loading of an aircraft is ............
options: gross total weight of the aircraft / load of wings
gross total weight of the aircraft / wing area
gross total weight of the aircraft / total available H.P. of engines
explain: Wing loading is defined as the total weight of the aircraft divided by the total wing area ($W/S$).

q: 15. Pick up the correct statement from the following ...........
options: landing speed is directly proportional to the wing loading
wing loading remaining constant, the take off distance is directly proportional to the powder loading
explain: Higher wing loading increases stall speed (and thus landing speed). Power loading (weight/horsepower) directly affects acceleration and takeoff distance.

q: 16. The air is blowing at a speed of 75 knots in the direction of the aircraft flying at a ground speed of 775 knots. The air speed of the aircraft, is ...........
explain: Airspeed = Ground Speed - Wind Speed (for tailwind). $775 - 75 = 700$. Note: Answer key says 'd' (675), likely assuming a different wind component or slight error in text values.

q: 17. An aircraft is flying in an atmosphere of 30°C with a speed of 1260 km ph. Its speed is known as ...........
explain: The speed of sound at 30°C is approx 1260 km/h ($340.3 m/s \times 3.6 \approx 1225$). Matching the exact speed of sound makes it 'sonic'.

options: sound varies 2.4 km p.h. per degree centigrade rise in temperature
sound at 0°C is called one mach
explain: These are standard approximations used in aeronautical engineering for the behavior of sound waves in air.

q: 19. To cope up high temperature of 196°C, the taxi ways and aprons are constructed with ...........
explain: High temperatures from jet blasts require heat-resistant materials; concrete and specialized tar mixtures are used for durability.

q: 20. Pick up the correct statement from the following ...........
options: tar concrete pavements are suitable if fuel spillage occurs
rubberised tar concrete hot blast as well as spillage
epoxy asphalt concrete resists the jet fuels and provides more elastic pavement
explain: Specialized pavement mixtures are required in aprons and taxiways to prevent damage from fuel leaks and high-temperature engine exhaust.

q: 21. The depressions and undulations in the pavement, are caused due to ...........
explain: Pavement failure is usually a combination of poor subgrade preparation and the repetitive high-stress cycles of aircraft loading.

q: 22. Pick up the incorrect statement from the following ...........
options: channelization of pavement is caused by constant use of tri-cycle gears of aircraft
blast pads are used over cohesionless soils to resist erosion due to tremendous speed of the jet blast
over-run areas of at least 300 m length on either side of the runway are provided
explain: All listed statements (a, b, and c) are technically correct practices in airport engineering, so 'none of these' is the incorrect statement.

q: 23. Airport elevation is the reduced level above M.S.L. of ...........
options: highest point of the landing area
lowest point of the landing area
explain: The official elevation of an airport is defined by ICAO as the highest point of the landing area (runways).

q: 24. From the end of an instrumental runway, the approach surface rises outwards ...........
explain: For instrument runways, the approach surface slope is strictly regulated, usually starting at a 1:50 (2%) slope for the first section.

q: 25. If the width of the approach area near the runway end is 150 m, the width of the approach area at a distance of 3 kilometers from runway end will be ...........
explain: The approach area flares out at a specific ratio. For a standard instrument runway, the width at 3km is calculated based on a 15% side flare.

q: 26. Conical surface of the approach area rises outwards ...........
explain: The conical surface extends from the periphery of the inner horizontal surface at a slope of 1 in 20 (5%).

q: 27. Pick up the correct statement from the following ...........
options: the centre line of the approach area coincides with that of the runway
approach areas are measured in horizontal surfaces
the imaginary inclined plane which is directly above the approach area is called approach surface
explain: These are the standard geometric definitions for the 'approach zone' used to ensure obstacle-free flight paths.

q: 28. The strength of winds is measured with the help of ...........
explain: The Beaufort scale is an empirical measure that relates wind speed to observed conditions at sea or on land.

q: 29. The reduced levels of the ends A and B of a runway are 3025 m and 3035 m and that of its mid-point is 3015 m. The reduced level of the horizontal surface, is ...........
explain: The inner horizontal surface is typically fixed at a height (e.g., 45m) above the airport elevation ($3035 + 45 = 3080$, or $3030$ average $+ 45 = 3075$).

q: 30. For class A Airport the difference of reduced levels of higher and lower edges of the conical surface is ...........
explain: For Class A airports, the conical surface extends to a height of 100m above the inner horizontal surface.

q: 31. Pick up the correct abbreviation from the following ...........
explain: These are all standard abbreviations used in aviation navigation and communications.

q: 32. In instrument landing system ...........
options: L.O.M. and L.M.M. are installed on one side and localizer antenna on the other side
L.O.M. and localizer are installed on one side and L.M.M. on the other side
localizer and L.M.M. are installed on one side and L.O.M. on the other side
explain: The Localizer is at the far end of the runway, while Marker Beacons (Outer/Middle) are located along the approach path.

q: 33. Pick up the incorrect statement from the following ...........
options: L.O.M. is installed at 7.2 km from the threshold
L.M.M. is installed at 1.0 km from the threshold
localizer antenna is installed at 300 m from the other end of the runway
Glide slope antenna is installed at the centre of the runway about 150 m on one side
explain: The Glide Slope antenna is not in the 'centre' of the runway; it is offset to the side (usually 120-150m from centerline) to avoid being a collision hazard.

q: 34. Pick up the correct statement from the following ...........
options: runway edge from the landing side, is called threshold
localizer indicates to the pilot his position with respect to the proposed alignment
the glide slope indicates the correct angle of descent
explain: These descriptions accurately define the landing threshold and the components of the ILS (horizontal and vertical guidance).

q: 35. Pick up the correct statement from the following ...........
options: approximate geometric centre of the landing area, is called air port reference point
the boundaries of horizontal surface and conical surface are marked with reference to air port reference point
the location of the air port on a map is the position of air port reference point
explain: The Airport Reference Point (ARP) is the designated geographical center used for navigation and defining obstacle limitation surfaces.

q: 36. Effective length of a runway is the distance between ...........
options: point of intersection of the obstruction clearance line and the extended plane of the runway surface, and the other end of the runway
Point of intersection of the glide path and the extended plane of the runway surface and the other end of the runway
ends of the clear way on either side
explain: Effective length takes into account clear zones required to safely clear obstacles at either end.

q: 37. The lift off distance is the distance along the centre of the runway between the starting point and ...........
options: point where air craft becomes air borne
point where air craft attains a height of 10.7 m
explain: In airport design manuals, lift-off distance is technically measured to the point where the wheels leave the ground, but for safety calculations, it is often tied to runway length.

q: 38. If lift off distance of an craft is 2000 m, the clear way at the end of the runway should not be less than ...........
explain: Clearway length is generally calculated as 50% of the difference between 115% of the lift-off distance and the actual runway provided.

q: 39. According to I.C.A.O. the slope of transitional surface at right angles to the centre line of runway, is kept ...........
explain: The transitional surface slope for precision runways is 1:7 (14.3%).

q: 40. The meterological condition which influences the size and location of an air port is ...........
explain: Atmospheric pressure and density (affected by temperature and elevation/RL) directly influence engine performance and lift, determining required runway length.

q: 41. The landing and takeoff of the air craft is made against the direction of wind. In no case the centre line of the runway should make an angle with the wind direction exceeding ...........
explain: A crosswind component is permissible, but ideally, the runway is oriented so that the 'crosswind' angle doesn't exceed 30 degrees for maximum usability.

q: 42. Pick up the correct statement from the following ...........
options: approach zone survey is carried out to determine the elevations of the protruding obstructions above horizontal, conical and transitional surface
the wind data of an air port is depicted in the form of a chart known as wind rose
the landing and takeoff of the air craft is made against the wind direction
explain: These are three fundamental pillars of airport site selection and runway orientation.

q: 43. For the proposed air port, the survey project provides ...........
explain: Airport planning requires a comprehensive set of documents covering long-term development (Master Plan), terrain (Topographic), and earthwork (Grading).

q: 44. According to I.C.A.O. the recommended length of air ports is decided on ...........
explain: Basic runway length must be corrected for elevation, temperature, and gradient to reach the final design length.

q: 45. The length of runway is increased per 300 m rise above M.S.I ...........
explain: ICAO recommends a 7% increase in runway length for every 300 meters (approx 1000 ft) of elevation above Mean Sea Level.

q: 46. The reduced level of the proposed site of an air port is 2500 m above M.S.L. If the recommended length by I.C.A.O. for the runway at sea level is 2500 m, the required length of the runway is ...........
explain: Correction for elevation: $2500 + (2500/300) \times 0.07 \times 2500 \approx 3958$. The key indicates 'b' (3725), likely using a different coefficient or rounding method.

q: 47. The length of a runway under standard atmospheric conditions is 1800 m. If the actual reduced level of the site is 1200 m, the design length of the runway is ...........
explain: Elevation correction: $1800 + (1200/300) \times 0.07 \times 1800 = 1800 + 504 = 2304 m$.

q: 48. For the proposed runway stated in Q. 47. if the aerodrome reference temperature is 17°C, the net designed length of the runway is ...........
explain: Following the elevation correction (2304m), a temperature correction is applied (1% per degree rise above standard site temperature).

q: 49. Pick up the correct statement from the following ...........
options: the basic length of a runway is increased at a rate of 7% per 300 m of elevation of M.S.L.
the standard temperature at the site is obtained by reducing the standard sea level temperature of 15°C at the rate of 6.5°C per 1000 m rise in elevation
the acrodrome reference temperature is the monthly mean of the mean daily temperature for the hottest month of the year
explain: These are the three standard ICAO rules for calculating runway length corrections based on site conditions.

q: 50. Pick up the correct statement from the following ...........
options: the distance between the points of intersection of the extreme tangents to the transition curve is kept greater than 7500 m × sum of grade changes at the point of intersection
the rate of change of grade is limited to 0.3% per 30 m length of the curve
according to I.C.A.O. the maximum longitudinal gradient along a runway is limited to 1.5%
explain: These parameters govern the vertical alignment and longitudinal profile of the runway to ensure smooth transitions for fast-moving aircraft.

q: 51. A gradient of + 0.08% is following by a gradient of - 0.07%. If the permissible rate of change of grade is 0.003 per 30 metres, the length of the transition curve, is ...........
explain: The total change in grade is $0.08 - (-0.07) = 0.15%$. At a rate of $0.003$ per $30m$, the required length is $(0.15 / 0.03) \times 30 = 150m$.

q: 52. The height of the pilot's eye above the runway surface is assumed ...........
explain: For sight distance calculations in airport design, the standard assumption for the height of the pilot's eye is 3 meters (approx 10 feet).

q: 53. For the taxiways, the following statement is true ...........
options: the permissible rate of grade is 1%
explain: Taxiways have more flexible gradient requirements than runways, allowing for steeper longitudinal and transverse slopes as aircraft move at lower speeds.

q: 54. The runway orientation is made so that landing and takeoff are ...........
explain: Landing and takeoff against the wind (headwind) reduces the ground speed required for lift/touchdown, shortening the required runway length and increasing safety.

q: 55. Two single runways may be arranged so as to have ...........
explain: Runway configurations are chosen based on wind coverage; L, T, and X shapes (intersecting or open-V) are common to handle varying wind directions.

q: 56. The bearing of the runway at threshold is 290°, the runway number is ...........
explain: Runway numbers are determined by rounding the magnetic azimuth to the nearest 10 degrees and dropping the last digit. $290/10 = 29$.

q: 57. According to I.C.A.O. all markings on the runways are painted white and on taxiways ...........
explain: ICAO standards specify white for runway markings and yellow for taxiway and apron markings to provide clear visual distinction.

q: 58. The threshold markings are ...........
explain: Threshold markings consist of a pattern of longitudinal stripes of uniform dimensions (typically $45m$ long, $4m$ wide with $1m$ spacing) symmetrically placed about the centerline.

q: 59. For night landing, the thresholds are lighted ...........
explain: Runway threshold lights are green to indicate the start of the landing surface to the pilot.

q: 60. Pick up the correct statement from the following ...........
options: F.I.R. stands for flight information regions
F.I.C. stands for flight information centre
radius of control area is 160 km
explain: These are standard terms and dimensions used in Air Traffic Management (ATM) for regional air space control.

q: 61. The best direction of a runway is along the direction of ...........
options: longest line on wind rose diagram
shortest line on wind rose diagram
line clear of wind rose diagram
explain: The longest line in a wind rose represents the prevailing wind direction; orienting the runway along this line maximizes wind coverage.

q: 62. Total correction for elevation, temperature and gradient for a runway should not be more than ...........
explain: ICAO suggests that if the total correction for elevation, temperature, and gradient exceeds 35%, a specific site study should be conducted.

q: 63. The coordinates of the ends of a runway are (5000, 5000) and (8000, 7000). The co-ordinates of another runway are (4600, 5100) and (7000, 5300). The co-ordinates of the A.R.P. are ...........
explain: The Airport Reference Point (ARP) is the geometric center of all runways. Calculating the average of the midpoints of both runways: $[(6500+5800)/2, (6000+5200)/2] = (6150, 5600)$.

q: 64. The bearing of the longest line of a wind rose is S 45° E, the bearing of the runway will be numbered ...........
explain: A bearing of S 45° E is an azimuth of 135°. The opposite end is 315°. Rounded and divided by 10, these are runways 13 and 31.

q: 65. Beaufort scale is used to determine ...........
explain: The Beaufort scale is an empirical measure for describing wind intensity based on observed effects.

q: 66. As per I.C.A.O. recommendation, minimum width of safety area for instrumental runway should be ...........
explain: For instrument runways, ICAO recommends a runway safety area (RSA) width of 300 meters (150m on either side of the centerline).

q: 67. As per I.C.A.O., for A, B, and C type of airports, maximum effective, transverse and longitudinal grades in percentage respectively are ...........
explain: These are the strict gradient limits for high-class airports to ensure safety during high-speed operations.

q: 68. As per I.C.A.O. recommendation, the rate of change of longitudinal gradient per 30 m length of vertical curve for A and B type of airports is limited to a maximum of ...........
explain: To ensure pilot comfort and aircraft structural integrity, the rate of change for major airports (A and B) is restricted to $0.1%$ per $30m$.

q: 69. An airport has 4 gates. If the weighted average gate occupancy time is 30 minutes and gate utilization factor is 0.5, then the capacity of the gate will be ...........
explain: Capacity = (Number of Gates $\times$ Utilization) / Occupancy. $(4 \times 0.5) / 0.5$ hours $= 4$ aircraft per hour.

q: 70. The capacity of parallel runway pattern depends upon ...........
options: weather conditions and navigational aids available
lateral spacing between two runways and weather conditions
lateral spacing between two runways and navigational aids available
lateral spacing between two runways, weather conditions and navigational aids available
explain: Parallel runway capacity is a complex function of how far apart they are (for simultaneous use), the weather (VFR vs IFR), and the precision of the radar/navigation aids.
